title: IA3 activation scaling vs Mirror activation views
hypothesis: A shared base hidden gain plus pairwise orthogonal task views can represent aligned task activation functions at fewer bytes than IA3 while arbitrary gains require private state.
physical_object: Frozen shared 12x6 linear block and one base hidden gain vector
mirror_coordinate: Six per-task Givens angles, one per hidden-channel pair

optimization.mirror_fit: nonlinear least squares over shared gains and per-task angles

storage.serializer: uncompressed NumPy NPZ; Mirror base gain and packed angles stored in one view-code array

compute.active_compute_proxy: input projection plus hidden-output multiply; decode/materialization excluded from timing

success_gate: At least 3/4 fresh aligned worlds: Mirror MSE <=1.10x IA3, <=80% IA3 bytes, and better than shared gains.
failure_gate: Mirror MSE >1.25x IA3 in >=3/4 aligned worlds or matched-quality byte saving <10%.
